fullName: NIST AI 100-1 Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
note: All 72 subcategories across GOVERN/MAP/MEASURE/MANAGE. Verified against NIST AIRC Core (airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core). Optional sibling field `function` (Govern|Map|Measure|Manage) is permitted but not required.

valids.GV.1.1: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented
valids.GV.1.2: Trustworthy AI characteristics integrated into organizational policies
valids.GV.1.3: Processes determine needed risk management activity levels
valids.GV.1.4: Risk management process established through transparent policies
valids.GV.1.5: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of risk management planned
valids.GV.1.6: Mechanisms inventory AI systems per organizational priorities
valids.GV.1.7: Processes for safe decommissioning of AI systems
valids.GV.2.1: Roles, responsibilities, and communication lines documented
valids.GV.2.2: Personnel and partners receive AI risk management training
valids.GV.2.3: Executive leadership takes responsibility for AI risk decisions
valids.GV.3.2: Policies differentiate roles for human-AI configurations
valids.GV.4.1: Policies foster critical thinking and safety-first mindset
valids.GV.4.2: Teams document and communicate risks and impacts
valids.GV.4.3: Practices enable testing, incident identification, and information sharing
valids.GV.5.1: Policies collect and integrate external feedback on AI impacts
valids.GV.5.2: Mechanisms incorporate adjudicated feedback into system design
valids.MP.1.1: Intended purposes, beneficial uses, and deployment contexts understood
valids.MP.1.3: Organization's mission for AI technology understood
valids.MP.1.4: Business value or context clearly defined
valids.MP.1.5: Organizational risk tolerances determined and documented
valids.MP.1.6: System requirements elicited from relevant actors
valids.MP.2.1: Specific tasks and implementation methods defined
valids.MP.2.2: System knowledge limits and human oversight documented
valids.MP.2.3: Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations identified
valids.MP.3.3: Targeted application scope specified and documented
valids.MP.3.4: Operator and practitioner proficiency processes defined
valids.MP.3.5: Human oversight processes defined and documented
valids.MP.4.1: Approaches for mapping technology and legal risks in place
valids.MP.4.2: Internal risk controls for system components identified
valids.MP.5.1: Likelihood and magnitude of impacts identified
valids.MP.5.2: Practices for regular stakeholder engagement documented
valids.MS.1.1: Approaches and metrics for measurement selected
valids.MS.1.2: Appropriateness of metrics and controls regularly assessed
valids.MS.1.3: Internal experts and independent assessors involved regularly
valids.MS.2.1: Test sets, metrics, and tools documented
valids.MS.2.2: Human subject evaluations meet applicable requirements
valids.MS.2.4: System functionality and behavior monitored in production
valids.MS.2.6: System evaluated regularly for safety risks
valids.MS.2.7: Security and resilience evaluated and documented
valids.MS.2.9: AI model explained, validated, and documented
valids.MS.2.11: Fairness and bias evaluated and documented
valids.MS.3.1: Approaches track existing and emergent risks
valids.MS.3.2: Risk tracking approaches considered for difficult assessments
valids.MS.3.3: Feedback processes for reporting problems established
valids.MS.4.1: Measurement approaches connected to deployment contexts
valids.MS.4.2: Measurement results informed by relevant actors
valids.MG.1.1: Determination made on system achievement and proceeding
valids.MG.1.2: Risk treatment prioritized by impact and likelihood
valids.MG.1.3: Responses to high-priority risks developed and documented
valids.MG.2.1: Resources account for viable non-AI alternatives
valids.MG.2.2: Mechanisms sustain value of deployed systems
valids.MG.2.3: Procedures respond to previously unknown identified risks
valids.MG.2.4: Mechanisms supersede or deactivate underperforming systems
valids.MG.3.2: Pre-trained models monitored as part of maintenance
valids.MG.4.3: Incidents communicated and tracking processes documented
